- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 80+ values), then undercorrects or lags in subsequent days.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or failure to capture late-period momentum.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than true price movements, missing volatility spikes or sudden drops.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent history — especially when true values rise sharply, forecast doesn’t catch up until 2–3 days later.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model often overreacts with a peak that exceeds true outcome, then gradually corrects.
- Model underestimates when true values are near or below 80, especially in the last 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Forecast tends to be biased toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent high prices (e.g., >82).
